items.title: Global South–Canada Mining & Technology Transfer Mission
items.venue: Concludes at the Canadian Mining Expo, Timmins
items.description:
Every June, government and industry delegations from across the Global South come to Greater Sudbury, home to one of the world’s leading mining ecosystems. Over several days, delegates tour working mines and visit equipment and service suppliers, technology developers and research institutions. They meet the people behind them.

The mission is about more than seeing. It is about building lasting partnerships. Delegates come looking for proven Canadian expertise, technology and training that they can adapt to mining in their own countries. Their Canadian hosts, in turn, find new markets and long-term collaborators.

The mission then travels north to Timmins and ends at the Canadian Mining Expo, where delegates meet Canada’s wider mining supply chain in one place.

The 2027 mission takes place in the first week of June.

Co-hosted by LDII and Thrive Tours Inc., an Indigenous-led experiential tourism and education company based at Batchewana First Nation. The Sudbury programme covers the story of the city’s regreening, mining innovation including automation, battery-electric equipment and research at Laurentian, Cambrian and NORCAT, and business-to-business meetings with local mining suppliers and service companies.

items.title: Cultural Resilience One Planet Conference (CROP) 2026
items.description: Exploring the vital role of cultural heritage and traditional knowledge in building community resilience and sustainable development. This unique conference brings together cultural practitioners, Indigenous leaders, researchers, and policy makers to examine how cultural assets can strengthen community resilience against global shocks while preserving invaluable heritage for future generations.

This landmark event in Ontario will examine cultural preservation strategies, indigenous-led climate adaptation, and the role of arts in healing communities affected by global shocks.

items.title: 2nd International Post-COVID-19 Conference
items.description:
Economic Damages from Global Shocks: Building Resilience for the Future.

Global shocks such as pandemics, natural disasters and financial crises can have far-reaching and devastating effects on economies around the world. Their impact cuts across trade, finance and industry, leading to widespread job losses, slower economic growth and rising poverty.

Measuring the full extent of this damage is difficult because these shocks are complex and interconnected. At the Pearson Convention Centre in Brampton, the 2nd International Post-COVID-19 Conference brought together partners, policymakers, researchers and community leaders. They examined these effects, shared lessons from the pandemic and explored practical paths toward recovery and long-term resilience.

Over three days, discussions focused on how communities, businesses and institutions can better prepare for and respond to future shocks. The goal was to protect livelihoods and strengthen partnerships across borders.

Local Impact. Global Partnerships.
items.shortDescription: Economic damages from global shocks and building resilience for the future — partners, policymakers, researchers and community leaders in Brampton, Ontario.

items.title: COVID-19 Remembrance Parade & Candlelight Vigil
items.description: The world’s first COVID-19 Remembrance Parade and Candlelight Vigil, organized by LDII under the theme “Walking for Humanity, Healing, and Compassion, with Unity, Hope, and Renewal Beyond COVID-19.” Participants representing nations from around the world walked from Christie Pits Park, led by St. Andrews Pipes & Drums, before a candlelight vigil.

items.title: 1st International Post-COVID Conference
items.description: LDII's inaugural international conference, held at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre from July 11 to 13, 2024, under the theme Evaluating the Impact of COVID-19 on Humanity: Building Synergies and Resilience for Future Global Shocks. The Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) took part as co-convener and co-organizer, and delegates came from African Union member states, regional blocs and Canadian universities.
